title: PokerPal Wiki
text: Everything about using PokerPal, the poker session tracker for iPhone: logging cash games and tournaments, running a live session, recording hands, reading your statistics and keeping your bankroll in order. New here? Start with Your first session. Can't find an answer? Search above, read the FAQ or contact support.

title: Install PokerPal
text: PokerPal runs on iPhone with iOS 26 or later. Download First launch A short welcome walks you through reminders and shows what Pro adds. You can skip any step and change it later in Settings.

The Sessions tab with a list of cash games and tournaments Log a session you already played Tap New Session on the Sessions tab and answer the steps one by one: place, game, buy-in, cash-out, and when. title: Currency, places and stakes
text: Places A place is a casino, a club, a home game or an online room. Each place remembers its currency and your usual game. Currency Stakes and games Blinds and ante for cash games, the buy-in for tournaments, and the table size from heads-up to 10-max.

title: Add a session
headings: Log a game you play often
Can I change a session after saving it?
I don't remember how long I played. Does that affect my stats?
text: Log a session you've already played. You answer five short questions, and PokerPal works out your result. Usually, the only numbers you type are what you put in and what you took out. This guide follows one example evening: a $1/$3 cash game at Riverside Poker Room, $300 in and $742 out. Logging a cash game from the Sessions tab: adding a place, setting $1/$3 blinds, entering $300 and $742, and saving a $442 win Still playing? Use a live session instead. It keeps the clock and your buy-ins as you go. Start a new session 1. Open the Sessions tab. 2. Tap New Session. 3. Tap Log Session. The Sessions tab with two choices above the tab bar: Live Session and Log Session The screen that opens shows a short receipt at the top, with one line per question, and a panel at the bottom for the question you're on. The panel moves to the next question each time you answer. To change an answer, tap its line on the receipt. Step 1: Location Pick where you played. Your places are listed with the most recent first. The Where You Played panel listing Live Game, Online and a New Place button If you haven't saved any places yet, you'll see two general ones: Live Game and Online. Pick one of them, or add your own: 1. Tap New Place. 2. Type the name. 3. Choose Live Game or Online. 4. Check the Currency. A place remembers its currency, so future sessions there use it automatically. 5. Tap ✓. The new place panel with Riverside Poker Room typed in, Live Game selected and the currency set to USD Step 2: Game Choose what you played: Format: Cash, Tournament or SNG (a sit-and-go, a small tournament that starts when the seats fill). Game: NLHE (No-Limit Hold'em), PLO (Pot-Limit Omaha) and its five-card, six-card and Hi-Lo versions, Short Deck or Mixed. Tap Custom to add your own. SB and BB: the small and big blind. BB fills in at twice SB until you set it yourself, so for $1/$3 you enter both. Ante, the small bet everyone posts before a hand, is optional. Limit: No Limit unless you change it. Table: the number of seats, from 2 to 10. You can leave it unset. The Game panel with Cash and NLHE selected, SB set to 1 and BB set to 3 Blinds are worth filling in. They let PokerPal suggest buy-ins in the next step and show your results in big blinds (BB), the usual way to compare results across stakes. At $1/$3, one big blind is $3. For tournament fields, see Cash games and tournaments. Step 3: Invested Enter everything you put on the table: your first buy-in plus any rebuys, as one total. If you bought in for $300 and reloaded for $200, enter $500. The keypad with Total Invested showing $300, equal to 100 big blinds Once the big blind is set, the keypad offers 100 BB and 200 BB as one-tap amounts. Step 4: Received Enter the total you walked away with. The panel shows your result as you type. The keypad with Total Received showing $742, Invested $300 and Result plus $442 Two keys cover the common endings: Break Even enters the amount you invested. Busted enters 0. In a tournament, this key reads No Prize. Step 5: When The session is dated today unless you change it. Tap the left arrow to go back a day, then choose how long you played: Tap a length from 2 h to 8 h, and fine-tune it with −15 min and +15 min. Tap Not Known if you don't remember. The session is still saved, and you can add the time later. Tap Exact Time to enter when you started and finished, plus any breaks. The When panel with Today selected, length keys from 2 to 8 hours, and Not Known selected Check and save After the last step, you'll see your Net Result and the full receipt. Tap any line to change it. The summary screen showing a Net Result of plus $442 with the receipt and an empty Details section Before you save, you can fill in Details. This section is optional and holds: Tips and Expenses Hands Count Notes Online cash games show Tips only if you've already entered some. Tournaments have their own details, such as your finishing place and the field size. Your result is Received minus Invested, minus any tips and expenses that aren't already taken out of what you received. In this example, that's $742 − $300 = $442. When you've entered at least 15 minutes of play, the summary also shows your hourly rate, and in a cash game with blinds set, your big blinds per hour. Tap ✓ at the top right to save. The ✓ stays dimmed until Invested and Received are filled in. Your session then appears at the top of the Sessions list. The Sessions tab showing the saved session at Riverside Poker Room with a result of plus $442 Log a game you play often Once you've played two or more different games, Log Session opens with your Recent Games first. PokerPal lists up to five, newest first. The Recent Games list with Riverside Poker Room, Silver Creek Casino, Dave's Home Game and a Sunday Deepstack tournament Tap a game to fill in everything except the result and the time, then enter what you received. Tap New Game at the bottom to start from the receipt instead. If you skip this list, a new session still starts from your last completed one, with the same place, game and blinds. You only fill in the money and the time. Leave without saving Tap ✕ at the top left. If you've changed anything, PokerPal asks before throwing it away. Tap Discard to leave. Questions Can I change a session after saving it? Yes. Open it from the Sessions list. See Edit and delete a session. Why is the ✓ dimmed? Invested or Received is still empty. A cash game needs an Invested amount above 0. A tournament can be a freeroll, which means it's free to enter. I don't remember how long I played. Does that affect my stats? Your result counts as usual. The session just has no hourly rate, and PokerPal never assumes a length for you. What if saving fails? Your answers stay on the screen. Tap ✓ again, and you won't get a duplicate session.

title: Cash games vs tournaments
text: Cash games Profit is what you cashed out minus everything you bought in. Rates per hour and per 100 big blinds use the session's blinds. Tournaments You record the buy-in, the place you finished, the field size and the prize. Re-entries, add-ons, bounties and selling a share are Pro. Re-entries, add-ons, bounties, prize pools and selling a share of a tournament are part of Pro.

title: Record a hand
text: The hand recorder writes a hand street by street: seats, cards, actions and the showdown. Start a hand Tap Record a Hand on the Hands tab, or record one from a live session. The capsule at the top of the recorder shows the stakes, the game and the number of seats. Tap it to open Table Settings. Omaha (PLO) A PLO hand is recorded like a Hold'em hand, with four hole cards instead of two, five in PLO5 and six in PLO6. A hand from a session takes its game from the session. Without a session, open Table Settings and pick PLO, PLO5 or PLO6 in the Game row. The game is locked after the first card of the hero or a villain. The deck limits the seats: up to 9 players in PLO5 and up to 7 in PLO6. A villain's cards in PLO5 and PLO6 sit in two rows on the seat tile. In pot limit the size suggestions are shares of the pot, and the last button, Pot, is the maximum. A bigger amount is allowed with a warning, because the recorder writes down what happened at the table. The AI Review works for NLHE cash only for now, so Omaha hands don't have it. Actions Tags and notes

title: Smart Hand: dictate a hand
text: Smart Hand lets you dictate a hand in your own words. PokerPal turns it into a recorded hand and asks about anything it missed. How to dictate In Omaha, name all the cards of the hero and the villain: four, five in PLO5 and six in PLO6. You can name the game in the story, for example "PLO five". Say "pot" or "repot" without a number and the app works out the size. A hand from a session takes its game from the session, and dictation doesn't change it. Check and fix Privacy The recording is sent to a speech service to be transcribed only when you tap Send. See the Privacy Policy.

title: Statistics overview
text: The Statistics tab answers one question: where you win. The Statistics tab with net profit over time and key metrics All, Cash, Tournaments Filters Period, live or online, place and game. In Free, statistics cover the last 30 days. Pro opens any period, the filters and the breakdowns.

title: What each metric means
headings: Hourly rate in BB and BB/100
text: Net profit Everything you cashed out minus everything you put in, over the chosen period. Net hourly rate Net profit divided by the hours played. Hourly rate in BB and BB/100 Your result in big blinds per hour, and per 100 hands where hands are known. Winning sessions The share of sessions that finished above zero. ROI For tournaments: profit divided by the total buy-ins. ITM The share of tournaments where you finished in the money. Standard deviation per hour How much your hourly results swing. Drawdown The biggest drop from a peak in your results.

title: Your bankroll
text: Your bankroll is the money you keep for poker. Session results are added to it automatically; deposits and withdrawals you add yourself. Balance Deposits and withdrawals Low bankroll warning PokerPal compares your bankroll with your usual buy-in and warns you when the cushion gets thin.

title: Several bankrolls and currencies
text: Why several For example, one bankroll for live games and one for online, or one per currency. Transfers Currencies The first bankroll is free. More bankrolls and transfers between them are part of Pro.

title: Widgets and Live Activity
text: Home Screen widgets Lock Screen and Dynamic Island A running live session shows its clock and result on the Lock Screen. Controls

title: Limits and breaks
text: Limits you set for yourself. PokerPal never blocks anything; it tells you, at the right moment, when you reach a limit you chose. Stop-loss Breaks Monthly limit Tilt signal All of this is free.

title: Export to CSV
text: Export sessions Settings → Export Sessions. Pick a period and share a CSV file. Money is in each session's own currency. Opening the file Numbers, Excel and Google Sheets open the file directly.

title: Backups and sync
text: On your iPhone Your sessions, hands and bankrolls are stored on your iPhone. Backups Your data is included in your iPhone's iCloud or computer backup. Sync between devices PokerPal doesn't sync between devices yet.

title: Free and Pro
text: PokerPal is free to use. Pro shows why and where you win. What's free Logging cash games and tournaments, live sessions, one bankroll, statistics for the last 30 days, up to 10 recorded hands, CSV export, reminders and responsible play limits. What Pro adds Any period in statistics, breakdowns and the results calendar, more metrics and charts, unlimited hands, several bankrolls and currencies, tournament extras, the Lock Screen card and more widgets. Your data stays yours Everything you saved stays visible, editable and exportable after Pro ends.

title: Manage or restore a purchase
text: Manage or cancel Settings → Manage Subscription, or the Settings app → your name → Subscriptions. Restore a purchase Settings → Help → Restore Purchases. Refunds Refunds are handled by Apple at reportaproblem.apple.com.

title: FAQ
headings: How do I move my data to a new iPhone?
text: Is PokerPal a gambling app? No. PokerPal only records the games you play. It has no real-money games and no betting. Does PokerPal work offline? Yes. Everything except Smart Hand and Suggest an Idea works without the internet. Can I use several currencies? Yes. Each place and session keeps its own currency. How do I move my data to a new iPhone?
